propositions: MCP tool failures currently surface as unstructured prose in exception messages or ad-hoc partial shapes, preventing agents from reliably distinguishing error types such as ticket-not-found vs concurrency-mismatch vs gate-refusal
The CLI already emits a structured error_envelope discriminator (with error, input, message, exit_code fields) but only the CLI uses it; the library and MCP have no unified error-code vocabulary

A central classifier error_code_for(exc) must map all exception types to vocabulary codes and be sourced from a single KNOWN_ERROR_CODES registry, making the code stable regardless of human-message rewording and enforceable across library, CLI, and MCP interfaces

MCP must deliver the error_envelope (via McpEnvelopeError on Tool.__cause__) for every failure — both raised exceptions and the two existing soft-error return shapes (_mcp_reads explain_criterion, _mcp_llm) — while preserving existing agent-branching fields (kind, resolution_class, retryable, diagnostic)

TicketNotFoundError must be a new ReadError subclass raised only at the genuine not-found sites (reads.py:310/313) with the same message text, leaving the deps-reader not-found path unchanged so the CLI's message-keyed deps_failed vs ticket_not_found distinction remains byte-identical

The schema error_envelope.required field must be relaxed from [error, input, message] to [error, message] to permit target-less MCP failures (gate refusals) to omit input, while the CLI continues always emitting input so its output is unchanged
